criticalFindings.pattern: Invisible Bacterial Proliferation in High-Risk Cooked Foods
criticalFindings.explanation: Cooked rice, lentils, and pasta kept at room temperature (> 20°C) for over 12 hours develop hazardous levels of Bacillus cereus and other enterotoxins without dramatic visible discoloration or overt surface mold. Visual AI models rate them as Moderate or Fresh.
criticalFindings.systemMitigation: Enforce mandatory thermal-time check: If cooked food elapsed time > 4 hours in the temperature danger zone (4°C–60°C), the system must reject donation regardless of image visual rating.

criticalFindings.explanation: Apples and stone fruits with superficial skin bruising or dry superficial scars are frequently classified as 'Spoiled' by visual models, despite inner flesh being safe for cooking or trimming.
criticalFindings.systemMitigation: Provide donor guidance asking for cut-surface verification or allow donor confirmation of physical integrity.

failureCases.notes: High risk: Bacillus cereus heat-stable emetic toxin develops rapidly at room temperature. Visual inspection alone fails to detect invisible bacterial proliferation.
Fermentation bubbles in dal indicate active bacterial growth at tropical temperatures. AI vision can miss subtle froth without close-up inspection.

failureCases.foodName: Apple with brown internal rot around core (externally bruised)
failureCases.notes: External bruise looks severe to visual model, but flesh can be trimmed and fruit is still edible. AI over-penalized cosmetic bruising.

failureCases.foodName: Pasta with Marinara (left in pot at room temp for 24h)
failureCases.notes: Dried sauce layer masks internal bacterial colonization. AI predicts Moderate based on visible sauce color, missing the thermal danger zone violation.
